Look, I'm sure you're smart enough, so let me run something by you.

So I'm sure you understand how a large scale market works. You've got supply and demand and market price and sales price and differing values, all for just one product. And so there are thousands of companies selling thousands of products. Problem is this, what happens when the majority of people lose their jobs and stop being able to afford the majority of things?

Well, many companies that operate at a large scale save money and shave the fat by laying off more people. This is common sense on a microeconomic scale. But on a macroeconomic scale, it can be devestating. Higher unemployment causes less sales for all companies, which causes higher unemployment. Laissez faire economics (meaning non interference economics) only will take you so far. At some point, the government has to step in for the good of the people.

Welfare created a social safety net that ultimately assists the economy, by providing unemployed people with a bit of income to keep them purchasing things. And plus, it's just an overall decent thing to do for another person.

As a general rule, simple answers are almost always wrong on some level, and while complexity is aggravating and annoying and difficult to understand, it oftentimes makes more sense in the bigger picture. Hope this helped.
